messages.subject: Different type of distribution results in different log-likelihood
parts:
Dear Help desk,

We tried 2 different types of distributions for the same proportion response variables belong to  (0,1], including
  1. beta regression for y-0.001
  2. log-normal regression for y-0.001
And 2 binomial model for the same counts response variables, including
  1. binomial
  2. beta-binomial
The results of the inla shows greatly different for WAIC and log-likelihood, especial the beta regression. 

Also, some of my observations are (0,0), is there any way to include these data into my models? The Zeroinflatedbetabinomial is not working.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different type of distribution results in different log-likelihood
parts:
doing log-normal regression with proportion data could give different results
compared to beta-distribution, especially for the DIC/WAIC/marg.likelihood, as
the log-normal does not know that the response is in the interval <0,1>.

for the beta-distribution, then exact 0 is not allowed. the reason is that
observing exact 0, simply mean that the density at 0 cannot be zero (as its then
also 0 in the epsilon neigbourhood), hence this impose constraits on the
parameter values, including the linear predictor. (see parameter 'a', hence 'a'
must be <= 1 if I do the mental math correct...)
